digest.greeting: Good morning, Jean. Thursday, September 17 has 11 timed calendar entries, including a noon conflict, plus six carried-over items and four urgent tracked actions. The day turns on the Amazon Connect Wave 1 go/no-go decision, setting the CoE backlog and intake path after Sprint 18 filled, and launching the Attorney Review at Intake work with Jhara. The main risk is Amazon Connect: caller-ID control remains a two-to-three-week hard constraint, final setup capacity is tight before the planned September 22 pilot, and EPMO owns the enhanced-training mitigation. Dashboard completion state was last modified Friday, September 11, so carry-over status may be stale.

items.label: Make the Amazon Connect Wave 1 go/no-go decision
items.detail: Use today's risk review to decide whether the September 22 Columbus pilot can proceed. Caller-ID selection remains a two-to-three-week hard constraint, and final RingCentral setup capacity on September 18 and 21 is the other critical path.

items.label: Lock Amazon Connect production ownership and support
items.detail: Confirm the dedicated Salesforce integration account and the internal support model before production. SaltClick is still the de facto support owner, so the current plan carries single-point-of-support and additional-spend risk.

items.label: Set the CoE backlog and intake path for Sprint 19
items.detail: Coordinate the separate backlog review with Jill, notify CoE submitters that Sprint 18 is full, and make sure new requests are verified as EPMO or CoE work before scoping calls. Priorities will be reassessed every two weeks.

items.label: Clear the pending access approvals
items.detail: Decide Sara Rodriguez's Training Agenda access and review Armando's request in help desk ticket 0033237.

items.label: Clear the overdue Rippling task
